intervals.note: Start (1998) is the first data-taking run stated by the collaboration; the collaboration itself dates to 'the mid-1990s'. Data were taken only in the run periods listed as run intervals below. The end is the last data-taking run documented for the strange-form-factor programme (HAPPEX-III, 2009); no fetched source states an end date, and the collaboration went on to other parity-violation experiments (PREX, PVDIS, MOLLER: see experiment:prex and experiment:moller), which are recorded separately.
intervals.quote: Results were obtained in two separate data-taking runs, in 1998 and 1999 in Hall A at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility (Jefferson Lab).

name: HAPPEX apparatus (Hall A High Resolution Spectrometers)

placements.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2
placements.note: Campus-grade site (site:jlab-hall-a is the Hall A building footprint centroid). Dates as for the experiment: start = first run (1998), end = last documented run (2009).
placements.quote: The HAPPEx series of experiments were run in Hall A at Jefferson Lab

summary.plain: Hall A's two high-resolution spectrometers, which steer elastically scattered electrons onto detectors that integrate their signal during each beam-spin setting, with liquid-hydrogen or helium targets.
summary.technical: HAPPEX in Hall A: twin High Resolution Spectrometers (5 msr each in HAPPEX-III) focusing elastically scattered electrons onto total-absorption shower counters read out by integration over the helicity period; Compton and Moller polarimeters; superconducting septum magnets for the 6-degree HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He runs.

technology.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2
technology.quote: to focus elastically scattered particles onto a total absorption shower counter in each focal plane whose signals were integrated over the 33 ms helicity period
technology.value: Pair of Hall A High Resolution Spectrometers focusing elastically scattered electrons onto total-absorption shower counters whose signals are integrated over each helicity period
